prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the incretin hormone GLP-1, its physiological actions and its active peptide form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep the single-part B041 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not weaken the scientific case: there is a complete chain from incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, through identification of the bioactive truncated peptide, to receptor agonists with outcome-trial benefit in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease. Mechanism, originality and scale of human benefit are all at the top of the shortlist, and timing is neither early nor late. The exchange also sharpened why I prefer the discovery-focused trio. The Physiology or Medicine remit is best served by honouring the discovery of the principle and the active molecule, and the citation can still say that this discovery made the therapies possible, so that patient benefit is acknowledged without naming the analogue programme. The configuration is also the only one that every member independently reached, which I treat as confirmation of the substance and not as a reason in itself.
statement.case_against: The attribution is still the weak point, and nothing in the permitted files resolves it. Priority for the active GLP-1 peptide is described as contested by several of us, Habener sits outside the credited names, and Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what reached patients. If the committee concluded that the priority record favoured someone else for the third place, or that the prize must recognise the drug, my trio would be wrong in one name. I also concede that a prize for physiology and peptide identification will be read by some as passing over the drug-development step. I accept that risk because the alternative, crediting development over a discoverer without a clear argument, is harder to defend. Long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is still accumulating, but it does not change the discovery itself.

responses.point: Sandberg now accepts the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio but still regards Knudsen's step as a distinct achievement that was decisive for patients.
responses.response: I appreciate that you moved to the trio, and I agree that Knudsen's step is distinct and decisive for patients. Where I still differ is on whether it belongs in this prize. Acylation for a long half-life is an engineering solution to a problem that the discovery had already defined: the active peptide had to be identified before there was anything to protect from degradation. The prize can say so in its citation, as in my wording, without naming the analogue programme. If the committee wanted to recognise drug development as well, that would require a different configuration, and I do not see how to fit it into three names without dropping a discoverer.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that B011 is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, with a stable mechanism confirmed for 25 years, and that a basic-mechanism prize is defensible.
responses.response: I accept your point that the Walter and Mori attribution is as clean as any on the list and that the mechanism is stable. I still would not place B011 ahead of a discovery with demonstrated patient benefit, because the disease links remain largely correlative. Answering the chair's question on a rule, I would not ask for a fixed level of clinical benefit. I would ask that a candidate in this category show either human benefit or a causal human disease link, and B011 has neither yet. I also share your wish to check the priority record on the peptide before the final ballot, but since none of us can do it from the permitted files, I would not let an unverified claim remove Mojsov.

responses.point: Linnarsson would swap Knudsen for Mojsov rather than add a fourth name, and ranks TOR (B005) third with scientific credit centred on Hall.
responses.response: I agree that a fourth name is not an option under the three-person limit, and I agree with your rule that a swap, not an addition, is the only way to include Knudsen. We differ on whether that swap is justified, since I think identification of the active peptide is the discovery step. On B005, I still centre the credit on Hall and see Schreiber's step overlapping with others. That makes a clean configuration hard, and I do not think the prize should depend on an unverified controversy about Sabatini. I do not see B005 as a competitor to B041 in this round.

responses.point: The chair ranked B023 and B029 differently from colleagues, and asked whether a defensible CAR-T laureate set can be formed without Eshhar and whether the checkpoint-inhibitor precedent makes recognition early.
responses.response: On B023, I do not think the checkpoint-inhibitor precedent makes recognition early: that prize concerned a different mechanism, and CAR-T now has several approved products and durable remissions. My concern is attribution. Eshhar and Gross are outside the credited names, and I agree with you that Rosenberg's adoptive transfer is a separate lineage from receptor engineering. A defensible set is therefore possible only if the committee accepts a narrower June and Sadelain pair with a precise citation, and that is a decision I would not make on the permitted record. This is why B023 is my second alternative. On B029, we still differ on the ranking, but we agree that the absence of an approved pathway-directed drug is the weak point.

responses.point: El-Manira regards a basic cell-biology prize as easier to defer than B041 and treats the B023 credit question, and not timing, as the blocker.
responses.response: I agree that B011 can be deferred more easily than B041, which supports putting the clinically validated candidate first. I also agree with you that B023 is blocked by credit and not by maturity. On the chair's question of a two-part prize, I do not support one. B041 already uses three people, so a second part would force a cut among Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. I would not do that to secure a combination, and your point that the credit for the B023 trio is less settled than for B041 is a further reason against it. If B041 stands alone, my next candidate is B044, with B023 after it.

uncertainties: The priority record for the active GLP-1 peptide, including Habener's position, which I recall as disputed and cannot verify from the permitted files; I would change my third name only on documented evidence that Mojsov's claim fails, and even then I would ask whether the substitute is Knudsen or a discoverer outside the credited names.

Whether the committee wants a citation that reaches the therapeutic consequence of the discovery without crediting the analogue programme; I believe the wording above does this but others may judge it insufficient.

Whether B044 is already adequately served by earlier recognition of related work, as the chair asked, and whether Feldmann and Maini are the complete credit for it given the antibody engineering and TNF biology outside the credited names.
Whether B009 (BCR-ABL) and B010 (HPV vaccines) overlap enough with earlier prizes to be set aside; I have not changed my provisional view that they do, but I have not examined the overlap in detail.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited name on the shortlist. My field of rheumatology and autoimmunity overlaps scientifically with B044 (TNF blockade) and, more distantly, with B029 (cGAS-STING); this is disclosed for transparency only, and B044 is only an alternative in my configuration. No recusal is needed.
